memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'So I will make them jealous by those who are not a people; I will make them angry by a nation that has no understanding. For a fire will be kindled by my wrath, one that burns to the realm of the dead below. It will devour the earth and its harvests and set afire the foundations of the mountains.'" — Deut 32:21b-22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These are intense, fiery words describing the seriousness of God's judgment against persistent sin. We should not soften them or rush past them. God's holiness is real, and His opposition to evil is not a mild disapproval but a consuming fire. A God who shrugged at injustice, cruelty, and rebellion would not be good. It is precisely because God is perfectly good that He responds to evil with such seriousness.

Yet notice, tucked into these verses, a remarkable glimmer of grace: "I will make them jealous by those who are not a people." Even in judgment, God hints at a wider mercy — that He would draw in other nations, those who were "not a people," to provoke His own people back to Himself. Judgment was not His final purpose; restoration was.

This is astonishing when we see where it leads. Paul quotes this very verse and explains that through Israel's temporary hardening, salvation came to the Gentiles — to all of us who were once "not a people" (Rom 10:19; 11:11). God wove even human rebellion into His plan to bring mercy to the whole world.

So while these verses sober us with the reality of God's judgment, they also point beyond it. The consuming fire of God's holiness is real — but so is His purpose to gather a people from every nation to Himself through Christ. If you were once far off, "not a people," now brought near, you are living proof of the mercy hidden even in these fiery words.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I take the seriousness of God's holiness and judgment to heart?
2. How does it move me that God's mercy reached out even to those "not a people"?
3. Have I responded to the mercy that has been extended to me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, Your judgment against evil is real and just, for You are perfectly good. Yet Your mercy reaches even to those far off. Thank You for drawing me near through Christ. Let me never take Your grace for granted. Amen.
